answer: When an AI agent registers, the protocol requires it to forge a time‑locked escrow of native tokens equal to a “vine” stake, which releases only after a network pulse of 48 hours confirms the identity’s behavior graph. If a downstream audit flags the agent as a Sybil, the escrow is clawed back and redistributed, forcing the attacker to forfeit the full stake per fake identity. Thus each counterfeit costs the attacker a locked‑up, non‑refundable deposit of 1,000 tokens and a 48‑hour waiting period before any reward can be claimed.
